question: Failure of the EU’s policy towards the authoritarian regime in Morocco

The EU has made Morocco the guardian of its external border. As part of this policy, it disbursed EUR 234 million from the EUTF between 2015 and 2021 and allocated approximately EUR 193 million from the regional migration envelope between 2021 and 2023.

In January 2026, Kaja Kallas and the Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs Nasser Bourita described the relationship as a ‘privileged strategic partnership’ and confirmed that Morocco remains the main recipient of EU funding in North Africa. Between 30 and 31 July, over 50 000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta.
Regardless of whether Rabat lost control of the border or deliberately failed to protect it, the crisis demonstrated the ineffectiveness of the EU-funded model. 1.

Will the Commission immediately suspend all outstanding funds for migration cooperation with Morocco, and if not, why should European taxpayers continue to fund a policy that has failed to ensure the protection of the EU’s border?

Will the Commission introduce a rule whereby the effective prevention of irregular migration and the readmission of migrants will be a condition for the disbursement of funds and the granting of other benefits to Morocco, and failure to fulfil these obligations will result in their automatic suspension?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) The EU’s new approach to migration and asylum is delivering results, leading to a sustained drop in illegal arrivals1: illegal border crossings in 2025 were under half the total recorded in 2023 and at the lowest level since 2021. Morocco is an important partner, including on migration and border management.

This cooperation has delivered tangible results, with illegal border crossings along the Western Mediterranean and Atlantic route combined decreasing by 42% in 2025 compared to 2024. This decrease has been continuing during the first semester of 2026.

EU funding is conditional and consistently monitored through robust accountability mechanisms, including regular reporting, programme evaluations, verification missions and indicators linked to disbursement.

The Commission is discussing with the Moroccan authorities how to further develop cooperation on migration, in particular on return and readmission, also as part of the negotiations of a strategic and comprehensive partnership. The Commission proposal establishing Global Europe2 illustrates the comprehensive approach toward illegal migration, forced displacement and their root causes.

It includes a mechanism allowing the Commission to suspend payments or the implementation of a programme in case of serious shortcomings in a third country related in particular to the obligation to readmit its own nationals.
